output.summary: A shrub or small tree native to the southwestern United States and adjoining northern Mexico, New Mexico locust has bristly shoots, sharp reddish-brown thorns, and showy white or pink flowers. Pueblo Native Americans in New Mexico traditionally ate the flowers uncooked, while some Mescalero and Chiricahua Apache ate the pods raw or cooked.
